title: Simulate preference labels
description: This code labels three response pairs and computes their naive preference win rates.

steps.description: preference_pairs holds three prompts with response A and response B for each.
ground_truth_preferred supplies one hardcoded label per pair. A value of 1 means response A is preferred.

steps.question: Which response is preferred for every pair under these labels?
steps.answer: Response A is preferred for all three pairs.

steps.description: The loop names the preferred and rejected response for each pair and records their naive reward counts.
The summary prints response A as preferred and response B as rejected for each prompt.
The code sums the preference labels to calculate total wins and a win-rate score for A and B.
The output gives response A 3 out of 3 wins and a score of 1.00, while response B has 0 out of 3 and a score of 0.00.
The printed explanation distinguishes this count from a reward model trained on chosen and rejected response triples.
